basis: Immune-complex deposition defines the renal disease; hypertension is a secondary complication, and extra-renal inflammatory manifestations are uncommon.
Neurologic syndrome with cognitive and autonomic dysfunction; fatigue and myalgia do not establish muscle damage, and immunodeficiency is not a defining established mechanism.
Inherited retinal degeneration; no established common extraocular damage.
Biphasic malignant tumor originating in the lung.
Entrapment neuropathy of abdominal cutaneous nerves; abdominal pain does not indicate gastrointestinal disease, and vertigo alone does not establish vestibular damage.
Syndromic hearing loss; sperm abnormalities and male infertility involve reproductive functions outside the axes, without established endocrine dysfunction.
Benign neoplasms of the peripheral nervous system; endocrine or other organ origins occur only in particular subtypes.
Pituitary hormone deficiency and immunodeficiency define disease; alopecia/nail dystrophy occur in 30-79%; bronchiectasis and recurrent infections are separate secondary diseases.
ACTN4-related glomerular disease; anemia, hypertension and fluid accumulation are secondary complications, and a single severe case does not establish common extra-renal damage.
Congenital joint fusion defines disease; stapes ankylosis with conductive hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%.
Retinal dystrophy with characteristic flecks and frequently mild stationary night blindness.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; renal dysplasia, hydrocephalus and intestinal malrotation each reported in 1/2 patients. Frequencies derive from a very small series.
Elbow, wrist and digit skeletal dysplasia defines disease; structural fingernail abnormalities are reported in 80-99%.
Severe limb and pelvic skeletal malformations define disease; nail dysplasia occurs in 80-99%. Genital malformations fall outside the axes.
KMT2A-rearranged acute myeloid neoplasm of blood and marrow; no established common direct extrahematologic involvement.
Umbrella concept explicitly defined by disease of the dermis.
Characteristic BAP1-inactivated melanocytic skin tumors are a defining manifestation; associated visceral cancers are separately diagnosed tumors, not automatic organ involvement.
Mature B-cell leukemia/lymphoma involving hematolymphoid tissues; the lymphoma component warrants the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Ulceration is confined to vulva/vagina; association with preceding infection does not establish direct infection or a defined autoimmune disease.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines syndrome; supplied HPO reports aortic aneurysm in 80-99% and congenital diaphragmatic muscle defects in 30-79%.
Peripheral neuropathy classified as a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder; weakness and foot deformity reflect denervation rather than a separate primary myopathy.
Behavioral and cognitive syndrome caused by bilateral temporal brain damage; infectious and traumatic causes vary, so infection is not intrinsic to the syndrome.
Skin, hair, nail and dental dysplasia define disease; ptosis and eyelid abnormalities occur in 30-79%.
TPM2-related skeletal myopathy with weakness, contractures and nemaline bodies; motor delay reflects muscle disease. Psychiatric findings have no axis; seizures are uncommon.
Autoimmune platelet destruction; petechiae/purpura are bleeding signs. Arterial thrombosis is a separate complication, and the supplied 30-79% frequency is not clinically credible.
